interpretation: The PEtab nominalValue point is NOT this problem's published optimum, so it validates nothing about optimality. Its eight acetylation rate constants ARE the published maximum-likelihood estimates of Table S1/S2 in Blasi et al. (2016), but nominalValue for the noise scale is a placeholder sigma = 0.1, whereas the published fit profiles sigma to its maximum-likelihood value 0.2532. That single parameter accounts for the whole OG_nominal = 447.7. Holding the eight published rate constants and profiling sigma gives J_paper = -1090.5611, i.e. OG = 0.00075 -- so the benchmark's J* IS the paper's published motif-specific fit, and PyBNF's objective reproduces it. This slug's status comes from an actual fit (OG = -4.3e-07), not from this point.

objective_at_published_fit.note: The same Gaussian-on-natural-log NLL evaluated at the eight published Table S2 rank-1 rate constants, with sigma at its profile maximum-likelihood value sqrt(sum(residual^2)/n). Confirms that the benchmark's J* is the paper's own published fit; the residual 7.5e-04 is the four-digit rounding of the published rate constants.

independent_numpy_check.note: Gaussian-on-natural-log negative log-likelihood rebuilt in NumPy from the PEtab measurement table and a steady state solved as a null-space problem, evaluated at the same nominal point.
